manual_notes: The coordination provider has concrete narrow lock/KV/revision/event/health interfaces, memory and Redis implementations, token-checked TTL locks, Redis-native KV operations and atomic revision increments, namespaced tenant keys, event publication/subscription and health snapshots. Cache revision reads provide the missed-event fallback. Production Redis imports were located in the provider implementation; test helpers also import the client. Evidence supports implementation, not successful execution of every fault scenario.

sources.observed_facts: Public aliases expose the narrow service/store contracts and memory/Redis constructors.
SETNX with TTL acquires a token-bearing handle; owner-check Lua renew/release prevents old holders deleting a new lock; INCR provides fencing tokens.
Get/Set/SetNX/Delete/CompareAndDelete/IncrBy/Expire/TTL use context-aware client operations and structured errors.
Shared revisions use atomic Redis INCR and scoped keys.
JSON event publication and context-bound subscription dispatch are implemented.
Ping and operation health track backend, last success, errors and subscription status.
Central key builder includes application/environment/instance and tenant/business dimensions.

Local revision branch and shared coordination store calls, tenant/cascade scoping, event payloads, revision fallback, freshness window, observable status and structured publication errors are implemented.
